title: Spread of the Neolithic into Europe
summary: Farming reached Europe from the Near East and Anatolia over several thousand years, between about 8000 and 3000 BCE by one estimate. Ancient DNA shows early farmers in central Europe were genetically close to Near Eastern and Anatolian populations, with genetic distances rising westward across the Balkans. Models favour movement of people over spread of ideas alone, with only limited mixing with local hunter-gatherers.

uncertainty.note: Sources give 8,000-4,000 b.c. for the transition (Haak et al.) and 8000-3000 BCE for the spread model (Isern et al.). The record id year (-7050) is an approximate marker only.

where.modern_name: Aegean Sea, used as a marker only; the spread ran from Anatolia across the Balkans and the Mediterranean
where.historical_name: Anatolia, Aegean and the Balkans on the route into Europe

importance.justification: Introduced farming across Europe, the base of later European settled societies.
